transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
Police say two people were hospitalized
following a shooting at an elementary school
in Bend, Oregon, and the shooter is dead.
Earlier, the Bend-Lapine School District
said on social media that there was an act
of lockdown at the school and that police were on the scene.
President Trump has canceled the live stream
of the firing squad execution of the Fort Hood shooter,
Nadal Malik Hassan, in part because it might fuel
violent extremism, NPR's Quill Lawrence reports.
The president was persuaded that it was against
American values to live stream an execution,
according to a US official who spoke on condition
of anonymity out of fear of retribution.
The official said Trump was also told the video
might be used to recruit violent anti-US extremists,
even putting US troops deployed to the Middle East at risk.
Nadal killed 13 fellow soldiers, including a pregnant woman,
on Fort Hood in 2009.
He was wounded in the aftermath and now uses a wheelchair.
A separate US official on Capitol Hill,
who was not authorized to speak publicly,
told NPR that it was Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth
who called for the firing squad to be televised,
quote, "catching everyone by surprise."
Quill Lawrence, NPR News.
- Immigration agents seized Minnesota Democratic Congresswoman
Ilhan Omar's personal documents and devices.
NPR's Luke Garrett reports that Omar was home
during the search.
Representative Omar's phone, personal computer,
passport, and notebooks were all taken by federal agents
on Monday, according to a person familiar with the case,
but not authorized to share details publicly.
Homeland Security investigation agents searched her DC home
as part of what the Justice Department calls
a federal criminal investigation.
A government official who spoke on the condition of anonymity
because they're not authorized to discuss the case
tells NPR that the Congresswoman was at her DC home
during the execution of the search warrant,
but was not detained during the hours-long visit.
Since Monday, members of Omar's family have been subpoenaed
in a case that centers on immigration fraud allegations.
Omar has long denied these claims
and calls the search of her DC home political targeting.
Luke Garrett, NPR News, Washington.
- Rising inflation is straining household budgets.
NPR's Windsor-Johnson reports people across the US
have collectively spent about $82 billion more on gasoline
since March than they did a year ago.
That estimate comes from the latest calculation
by gasbuddy.com.
Patrick DeHaan is head of petroleum analysis.
He says those extra fuel expenses are leaving families
with less to spend on holiday meals and gifts.
He also says booking holiday flights now
won't spare travelers from higher fuel costs.
- The airlines are having to pass this along.
So, you know, you can't avoid the increase in fuel
when what comes out of a barrel
is fueling the entire US economy.
You can't escape it.
- Heavy, bulky goods, including Thanksgiving turkeys
and perishable foods are especially vulnerable
to higher shipping costs.
Windsor-Johnson, NPR News.
- US stock indexes rose today.
You're listening to NPR News.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney says
there couldn't be a worse time for Alberta's vote
on a referendum that could set the province on a path
toward a future vote on separation from Canada.
The vote is not a direct referendum on independence.
Carney's remarks come amid President Trump's trade war
and repeated threats to make Canada the 51st state.
Israel says commercial goods have not entered Gaza
for the last several days.
It's blaming Hamas for imposing high taxes
on Palestinian merchants.
NPR's Daniel Estrin reports.
- Israel says merchants in Gaza refuse to import goods
because Hamas imposed high taxes and threatened merchants.
Hamas called it a voluntary payment.
- Because of the crisis, commercial goods
did not enter Gaza over the last two days,
cutting off about 50% of all shipments
of essential items to Gaza.
Market prices in Gaza have skyrocketed.
Shayna Lowe of the Norwegian Refugee Council Aid Group.
- Any disruption to the flow of goods,
whether they're humanitarian or commercial,
is a shock to the system in Gaza.
- In Gaza, a Palestinian trucker's union blamed Israel
for halting the shipments.
Gaza's two million people face a humanitarian crisis
with Israeli restrictions on aid supplies.
Daniel Estrin, NPR News.
- The Michigan Department of Natural Resources
has begun using genetic testing to track the success
of its fish stocking operations.
Using 23andMe type testing, the method helps determine
if fish in a water body descended from stock fish
were born naturally, helping inform future stocking decisions.
This is NPR News from Washington.

topics.text: Two people hospitalized after shooting at elementary school in Bend, Oregon; shooter dead
Trump cancels live stream of Fort Hood shooter Nadal Hassan's firing squad execution
Immigration agents seize Rep. Ilhan Omar's devices and documents in search of DC home
Americans spent about $82 billion more on gasoline since March, per GasBuddy estimate
Canadian PM Mark Carney criticizes timing of Alberta independence referendum vote
Israel says no commercial goods entered Gaza for two days, blames Hamas taxes on merchants
Michigan DNR uses genetic testing to track success of fish stocking operations
